IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT 
NAINITAL
Exemption Appl. No.01 of 2026
In 
Criminal Appeal No.15 of 2026
Jasvinder Singh ...Appellant 
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ...Respondents
Presence: Mr. Kapil Sibal, learned Senior Counsel, assisted by Mr. Nikhil Pahwa, learned 
 counsel and Mr. Vikas Kumar Guglani, learned counsel for the Appellant.
Mr. J.S. Virk, learned DAG, assisted by Mr. Rakesh Kumar Joshi, learned 
 Brief Holder, for the State of Uttarakhand.
Hon’ble Ashish Naithani, J.
The present application has been filed by the Appellant seeking 
exemption from surrender pursuant to the judgment and order dated 
22.12.2025 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge (Third), 
Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar, in Sessions Trial No. 164 of 
2018, whereby the Appellant has been convicted and sentenced.
2. Learned senior counsel appearing for the Appellant submits that 
the Appellant has preferred the present criminal appeal challenging the 
conviction, that arguable issues arise for consideration, and that the 
Trial Court had granted time to surrender. It is contended that 
insistence on surrender at this stage would cause irreparable prejudice 
to the Appellant.
3. Learned counsel for the State opposes the application, 
contending that once a person stands convicted, the normal rule is 
custody, and exemption from surrender is not a matter of course. It is 
submitted that the statutory framework does not contemplate such an 
exemption, and that the Appellant must submit to the consequence of 
conviction unless the sentence is suspended in accordance with law.
4. It is further submitted that, since the Appellant has not appeared 
after conviction and has been recorded as absconding, notices have 
1
Criminal Appeal No.15 of 2026 Jasvinder Singh vs. State of Uttarakhand.
Ashish Naithani J. also been issued to the persons who stood as sureties for the 
Appellant.
5. The Court has heard learned counsel for the parties and perused 
the record.
6. The power of the appellate court to suspend the execution of the 
sentence and to release a convicted person on bail during the 
pendency of an appeal is a statutory power traceable to Section 430 of 
the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
7. Significantly, neither the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 
2023, nor the earlier Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, contains any 
provision that contemplates “exemption from surrender” after 
conviction. The statutory scheme is clear; once a conviction is 
recorded and a sentence is imposed, the sentence becomes operative 
immediately, unless its operation is stayed or suspended by the 
competent court in exercise of statutory power.
8. The law draws a clear distinction between the pre-conviction 
and post-conviction stages. Prior to conviction, the presumption of 
innocence operates and liberty is the rule. Upon conviction, however, 
custody becomes the norm, and liberty can be claimed only through 
the statutorily recognised mechanism of suspension of sentence and 
consequential release on bail. Grant of exemption from surrender, in 
the absence of suspension of sentence, would effectively neutralise the 
conviction and disturb the statutory balance between trial and 
appellate stages.
9. The Hon’ble Supreme Court in Daulat Singh v. State of Madhya 
Pradesh (order dated 30.07.2024)Special Leave Petition (Criminal) 
Diary No(s). 20900/2024, has categorically observed that the Code 
does not contemplate an application seeking exemption from 
surrender pending appeal or revision and has cautioned against 
expanding inherent powers to permit such relief, particularly where 
findings of guilt have already been recorded. The Supreme Court has 
2
Criminal Appeal No.15 of 2026 Jasvinder Singh vs. State of Uttarakhand.
Ashish Naithani J. further emphasised that a person released on bail prior to conviction 
cannot insist on remaining at liberty after conviction unless the 
sentence is stayed or suspended by a competent court.
10. In the present case, the Appellant stands convicted after a full￾fledged trial. At this stage, granting exemption from surrender would 
amount to bypassing the statutory mechanism provided for suspension 
of sentence and would neutralise the effect of the conviction without 
judicial examination under the appropriate provision.
11. The record reflects that the Appellant was on bail during the 
course of the trial. Upon conviction and sentencing on 22.12.2025, the 
learned Trial Court cancelled the personal and surety bonds and 
granted time to surrender.
12. It is borne out from the record that subsequent to conviction, the 
learned Trial Court was constrained to issue a Non-Bailable Warrant 
on account of the Appellant’s non-appearance. The police report 
indicated that the Appellant was not found at the address furnished to 
the Court, leading to further coercive steps.
13. The plea of illness was raised before the Trial Court not by the 
Appellant himself, but through his surety on the basis of medical 
documents. The learned Trial Court, while taking such documents on 
record, did not suspend the sentence or dispense with custody and 
proceeded to secure the Appellant’s presence.
14. Apart from the above, this Court finds that the present 
application also suffers from a fundamental procedural defect. Rule 
3(4) of Chapter XVIII of Part III of the Rules of 1952 as applicable to 
Uttarakhand High Court mandates that in a case where a sentence of 
imprisonment has been awarded, the petition of appeal or the 
application for revision shall contain a certificate signed by the 
Advocate stating that the accused was not on bail or, if he was on bail, 
that he has surrendered. The relevant Rule reads as follows:
3
Criminal Appeal No.15 of 2026 Jasvinder Singh vs. State of Uttarakhand.
Ashish Naithani J. “3(4) In a case in which a sentence of imprisonment 
has been awarded the petition of appeal or the 
application for revision shall also contain a 
certificate signed by the Advocate for the appellant 
or the applicant, as the case may be, stating that the 
accused was not on bail or that, if he was on bail, he 
has surrendered. In a case in which bail has been 
granted by the Court appealed from under sub￾section (3) of Section 389 of the Code of Criminal 
Procedure, 1973, the fact shall be stated in the 
petition of appeal indicating the period for which 
such bail has been granted.”
15. The use of the word “shall” leaves no manner of doubt that the 
requirement is mandatory in nature.In the present case, the record 
reveals that the Appellant has not surrendered before the Trial Court, 
nor has the certificate as mandated under the Rules been annexed with 
the present proceeding.
16. In the absence of an order suspending the sentence, the 
Appellant is legally obliged to surrender and undergo the sentence 
imposed. Granting an exemption from surrender in such 
circumstances would be impermissible.
17. It is also material to note that the learned Trial Court, after 
considering the conduct of the Appellant and the material placed on 
record, fixed 17.01.2026 as the date for securing his presence, and 
issued consequential directions to the Senior Superintendent of Police 
for execution of the Non-Bailable Warrant, as well as to the concerned 
hospital to verify the medical claim.
18. In cases involving serious offences and severe sentences like 
that of the present matter, post-conviction custody is the rule, and any 
deviation therefrom must be strictly in accordance with statutory 
provisions. Granting exemption from surrender in such cases, without 
suspension of sentence, would undermine the discipline of criminal 
adjudication and erode public confidence in the administration of 
justice.
4
Criminal Appeal No.15 of 2026 Jasvinder Singh vs. State of Uttarakhand.
Ashish Naithani J. ORDER
19. In view of the aforesaid facts, statutory provisions, and settled 
principles, the application seeking exemption from surrender is 
rejected.
20. The application for suspension of sentence and enlargement on 
bail filed by the Appellant under Section 430 of the Bharatiya Nagarik 
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 shall be listed for consideration on 
25.02.2026. 
21. The Appellant is directed to surrender before the learned Trial 
Court forthwith, in accordance with law. It is clarified that such 
surrender shall not prejudice the consideration of the pending bail 
application.
(Ashish Naithani J.)
 (Vacation Judge)
 15.01.2026
Arti
5
Criminal Appeal No.15 of 2026 Jasvinder Singh vs. State of Uttarakhand.
Ashish Naithani J.

judgment and order dated 22.12.2025, 
passed in Sessions Trial No. 164 of 2018,

by the court of 3rd Additional Sessions 
Judge, Rudrapur, District Udham Singh 
Nagar. He has been convicted under

Section 25 (1-B) (A) of the Arms Act, 1959 
and sentenced accordingly. The appellant 
Jasvinder Singh seeks interim bail in this 
appeal on the ground of illness.
Heard on Interim Bail Application No. 
5 of 2026.
Learned Senior counsel appearing for 
the appellant submits that the appellant 
Jasvinder Singh is 68 years old man. He 
has been suffering with multiple diseases 
like systematic hypertension, Type-2 
diabetes, chest pain etc. He was admitted 
in Sushila Tiwari Government Hospital, 
Haldwani on 04.02.2026 and discharged 
on 09.02.2026. It is stated that the regular 
bail is already fixed on 10.03.2026.

ground of illness, the Court issue following

(i) In-charge of the concerned Jail 
shall ensure that the appellant 
is produced before the Head of

Hospital at the earliest, where 
the appellant shall be examined 
thoroughly.
(ii) In-charge, Sub-Jail shall follow 
the prescriptions given by the 
doctors in terms of medicines, 
died, checkups etc.
(iii) A detailed report shall be placed 
before the Court on 10.03.2026
(Siddhartha Sah, J.) (Ravindra Maithani, J.)

orders.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Bail Application (IA) No.2 of 2026
In
Criminal Appeal No. 15 of 2026
Jasvinder Singh ........Applicant/Appellant
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ……..... Respondent
Present : Mr. Siddharth Luthra, Senior Advocate (through video conferencing) 
 assisted by Mr. Vikas Kumar Guglani, Advocate for the
 applicant/appellant.
 Mr. J.S. Virk, Deputy Advocate General with Mr. Rakesh Joshi, Brief 
 Holder for the State. 
Coram : Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani. J.
 Hon’ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Instant appeal is preferred against the judgment and 
order dated 22.12.2025, passed in Sessions Trial No.164 of 2018, 
State of Uttarakhand vs. Angrej Singh alias Rinku and others, by 
the court of Third Additional Sessions Judge, Rudrapur, District 
Udham Singh Nagar. By it, the appellant has been convicted under 
Sections 302 read with 34, 120-B IPC and sentenced accordingly.
The appellant seeks bail during pendency of the appeal.
2. Heard on Bail Application (IA) No.2 of 2026.
3. According to the FIR, on 23.04.2018, some named 
persons had abused and threatened the brother of the informant 
PW1 Mohd. Khalid, asking him to leave the Transport Nagar area. 
Subsequently, on 03.05.2018 at 10:20 a.m., when PW1 Mohd. 
Khalid was with his brother and others at Kichha bye-pass, two 
motorcycle borne assailants, who had masked their faces, opened 
indiscriminate fire, due to which, deceased Sameer Ahmed was hit 
by 3-4 bullets and subsequently, he died.  2
4. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellant 
submits that the appellant has not been named in the FIR; all the 
named persons have been exonerated; the appellant was implicated 
in the case based on extra-judicial confession of the co-convicts 
allegedly made before PW4 Sahib Singh and PW5 Harjinder Singh, 
but both PW4 Sahib Singh and PW5 Harjinder Singh had not 
supported the prosecution case during trial; there is no other 
evidence against the appellant; the appellant was tried to be 
implicated on another link which is that the daughter of the 
appellant had transferred some money to a co-convict, who 
subsequently hired the shooters. It is submitted that the appellant 
has nothing to do with any transaction that has been made by 
Ramandeep Kaur, his daughter. 
5. Learned State Counsel does not dispute these factual 
narrations. 
6. Learned counsel for the informant also admits these 
factual narrations, but according to him, the conduct of the 
appellant may be relevant while deciding this application. He would 
submit that the judgment was delivered in the case on 22.12.2025, 
but on that date, the appellant was not present in the court.
Thereafter, for securing his presence, steps were taken by the court 
and subsequently, he surrendered.
7. In reply to it, on behalf of the appellant, it is argued 
that the appellant had filed appeal in the Court seeking Exemption 
From Surrendering Application No.1 of 2026, which was decided on  3
15.01.2026 and the appellant was directed to surrender before the 
trial court forthwith and accordingly, he surrendered. 
8. It is a stage of bail post conviction. Much of the 
discussion at this stage is to be avoided. To the extent of 
appreciating the controversy the matter may be examined with the 
caveat that any observation made at this stage shall have no 
bearing at any subsequent stage of the case and in as other case.
9. It is well settled law that the extra judicial confession is 
a weak kind of evidence. It is admitted at Bar that, in fact, the 
prosecution had initially relied upon the extra judicial confession 
allegedly made by the co-convict before PW4 Sahib Singh and PW5 
Harjinder Singh and it is also admitted that both PW4 Sahib Singh 
and PW5 Harjinder Singh have not supported the prosecution case 
at trial. Both the witnesses had stated that they had given their 
statements before the court as they were asked to depose by the 
police. In so far as money transaction is concerned, apparently
prosecution has not even shown that any money was transferred by 
the appellant. His daughter has allegedly transferred some money. 
If his daughter has transferred some money, what would be its 
effect that will find deliberation during hearing of the appeal. 
10. Having considered this and other attending factors, we 
are of the view that it is a case in which the execution of sentence 
should be suspended and the applicant/appellant be enlarged on 
bail.
11. The bail application is allowed. 4
12. The execution of sentence, which is under challenge in 
this appeal shall remain suspended during the pendency of the 
appeal.
13. Let the applicant/appellant be released on bail, during 
pendency of the appeal on his executing a personal bond and 
furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the 
satisfaction of the court concerned.
14. List along with connected matters.
 (Siddhartha Sah, J.) (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 10.03.2026 Sanjay
